blocks.value: Installs the OpenShift CLI in a container environment and perform compliance scan

inputs.name: playbook
inputs.value:
---
- name: Install OpenShift CLI (oc) and Deploy Compliance Operator
  hosts: localhost
  connection: local
  gather_facts: false
  
  vars:
    # OpenShift CLI installation vars
    oc_url: "https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/clients/ocp/latest/openshift-client-linux.tar.gz"
    oc_install_dir: "/tmp/oc-bin"
    ansible_remote_tmp: "/tmp/.ansible"
    kube_config_dir: "/tmp/.kube"
    
    # Compliance Operator vars
    compliance_namespace: "openshift-compliance"
    scan_binding_name: "compliance-scan"
    profile_name: "ocp4-cis"
    configmap_name: "ocp4-cis-api-checks-pod"
    
    # Retry parameters
    max_csv_retries: 30
    csv_retry_delay: 15
    max_configmap_retries: 10
    configmap_retry_delay: 30
  
  tasks:
    # OpenShift CLI Installation Tasks
    - name: Ensure the installation directory exists
      file:
        path: "{{ oc_install_dir }}"
        state: directory
    
    - name: Download OpenShift CLI archive
      get_url:
        url: "{{ oc_url }}"
        dest: /tmp/openshift-client-linux.tar.gz
        timeout: 120
      register: download_oc
    
    - name: Extract OpenShift CLI archive into installation directory
      unarchive:
        src: /tmp/openshift-client-linux.tar.gz
        dest: "{{ oc_install_dir }}"
        remote_src: yes
        extra_opts: ["--strip-components=0"]
      args:
        creates: "{{ oc_install_dir }}/oc"
    
    - name: Ensure the oc binary is executable
      file:
        path: "{{ oc_install_dir }}/oc"
        mode: '0755'
    
    - name: Get OpenShift CLI version
      command: "{{ oc_install_dir }}/oc version"
      register: oc_version
      changed_when: false
    
    - name: Display OpenShift CLI version
      debug:
        msg: "OpenShift CLI Version: {{ oc_version.stdout }}"
    
    # Create Kubernetes config directory
    - name: Create Kubernetes config directory
      file:
        path: "{{ kube_config_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'
    
    # Login to OpenShift Cluster
    - name: Login to OpenShift cluster
      shell: >
        KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config {{ oc_install_dir }}/oc login --server={{ ocp_api_endpoint }}
        --username={{ ocp_api_username }}
        --password={{ ocp_api_password }}
        --insecure-skip-tls-verify
      register: login_result
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: login_result.rc != 0
      environment:
        HOME: "/tmp"
    
    # Compliance Operator Installation Tasks
    - name: Create compliance namespace (idempotent)
      shell: |
        KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config {{ oc_install_dir }}/oc apply -f - <<'EOF'
        apiVersion: v1
        kind: Namespace
        metadata:
          name: "{{ compliance_namespace }}"
          labels:
            openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true"
        EOF
      register: ns_result
      changed_when: "'created' in ns_result.stdout or 'configured' in ns_result.stdout"
    
    - name: Check if Compliance Operator is already installed
      shell: "KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config {{ oc_install_dir }}/oc get subscription compliance-operator-sub -n {{ compliance_namespace }} --ignore-not-found"
      register: operator_subscription_check
      changed_when: false
    
    - name: Set compliance operator installed fact
      set_fact:
        compliance_operator_installed: "{{ operator_subscription_check.stdout != '' }}"
    
    - name: Debug operator installation status
      debug:
        msg: "Compliance Operator installed: {{ compliance_operator_installed }}"
    
    - name: Create OperatorGroup for Compliance Operator
      shell: |
        KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config {{ oc_install_dir }}/oc apply -f - <<'EOF'
        apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1
        kind: OperatorGroup
        metadata:
          name: compliance-operator-group
          namespace: "{{ compliance_namespace }}"
        spec:
          targetNamespaces: []
        EOF
      register: opgroup_result
      changed_when: "'created' in opgroup_result.stdout or 'configured' in opgroup_result.stdout"
      when: not compliance_operator_installed
    
    - name: Create Subscription for Compliance Operator
      shell: |
        KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config {{ oc_install_dir }}/oc apply -f - <<'EOF'
        apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1
        kind: Subscription
        metadata:
          name: compliance-operator-sub
          namespace: "{{ compliance_namespace }}"
        spec:
          channel: stable
          installPlanApproval: Automatic
          name: compliance-operator
          source: redhat-operators
          sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace
        EOF
      register: subs_result
      changed_when: "'created' in subs_result.stdout or 'configured' in subs_result.stdout"
      when: not compliance_operator_installed
    
    - name: Wait for Compliance Operator CSV to be ready
      shell: |
        export KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config
        current_csv=$({{ oc_install_dir }}/oc get subscription compliance-operator-sub -n {{ compliance_namespace }} -o jsonpath='{.status.currentCSV}')
        if [ -z "$current_csv" ]; then
          echo "No currentCSV found in subscription yet."
          exit 1
        fi
        csv_phase=$({{ oc_install_dir }}/oc get csv "$current_csv" -n {{ compliance_namespace }} -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' || echo "NotFound")
        if [ "$csv_phase" = "Succeeded" ]; then
          echo "CSV '$current_csv' is Succeeded."
          exit 0
        elif [ "$csv_phase" = "Failed" ]; then
          echo "CSV '$current_csv' has failed."
          exit 2
        else
          echo "CSV '$current_csv' is in phase: $csv_phase. Waiting..."
          exit 1
        fi
      register: csv_check
      retries: "{{ max_csv_retries }}"
      delay: "{{ csv_retry_delay }}"
      until: csv_check.rc == 0
      failed_when: csv_check.rc == 2
      when: not compliance_operator_installed
    
    - name: Delete existing ScanSettingBinding if it exists
      shell: "KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config {{ oc_install_dir }}/oc delete ScanSettingBinding \"{{ scan_binding_name }}\" -n \"{{ compliance_namespace }}\" --ignore-not-found"
      register: delete_binding
      changed_when: "'deleted' in delete_binding.stdout"
      ignore_errors: true
    
    - name: Apply ScanSettingBinding to initiate compliance scan
      shell: |
        KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config {{ oc_install_dir }}/oc apply -f - <<'EOF'
        apiVersion: compliance.openshift.io/v1alpha1
        kind: ScanSettingBinding
        metadata:
          name: "{{ scan_binding_name }}"
          namespace: "{{ compliance_namespace }}"
        profiles:
          - name: "{{ profile_name }}"
            kind: Profile
            apiGroup: compliance.openshift.io/v1alpha1
        settingsRef:
          name: default
          kind: ScanSetting
          apiGroup: compliance.openshift.io/v1alpha1
        EOF
      register: scan_binding_result
      changed_when: "'created' in scan_binding_result.stdout or 'configured' in scan_binding_result.stdout"
    
    - name: Pause for compliance scan stabilization
      pause:
        minutes: 2
    
    - name: Fetch ConfigMap details (retry up to {{ max_configmap_retries }} times)
      shell: "KUBECONFIG={{ kube_config_dir }}/config {{ oc_install_dir }}/oc get configmap \"{{ configmap_name }}\" -n \"{{ compliance_namespace }}\" -o yaml"
      register: configmap_output
      retries: "{{ max_configmap_retries }}"
      delay: "{{ configmap_retry_delay }}"
      until: configmap_output.rc == 0
      ignore_errors: true
      changed_when: false

    - name: Debug full ConfigMap response
      debug:
        var: configmap_output
    
    - name: Parse ConfigMap YAML
      set_fact:
        configmap_data: "{{ configmap_output.stdout | from_yaml }}"
      when: configmap_output.rc == 0

blocks.value: Convert the compliance scan results from JSON format to YAML format, which is required for further processing and ingestion.
Upload the compliance scan results to the Concert platform for further analysis and compliance tracking.

meta.description: This workflow automates the CIS compliance scan for OpenShift clusters using OSCO, ensuring that security policies are met. The scan results are transformed into a YAML format and uploaded into Concert for compliance tracking.
